candidates.name: Practice guide 40 supplement 4 - boundary agreements and determined boundaries
verified_facts: General boundaries are sufficient for most titles; a determined boundary records the exact line after it has been identified.
Determined-boundary plans should normally be prepared by a suitably qualified professional and must show sufficient surrounding detail and a stated scale, preferably no smaller than 1:200.
Measurement-based determined-boundary plans require horizontal measurements accurate to +/-10mm from defined permanent features.
National Grid coordinate-based plans require absolute accuracy +/-300mm and relative accuracy +/-10mm.
semantic_limits: These high-accuracy determined-boundary requirements do not turn ordinary HMLR title-plan or INSPIRE polygons into surveyed exact boundary coordinates.

candidates.name: Practice guide 40 supplement 1 - basis of HM Land Registry plans
verified_facts: Ordnance Survey mapping shows topographical features existing on the ground at survey time and is not intended to represent property boundaries.
HM Land Registry uses OS MasterMap as a basis for plans.
Typical plan scales vary by context, including 1:1250 urban, 1:2500 rural and 1:10000 mountain/moorland.
semantic_limits: A mapped physical feature or map scale cannot be promoted to exact legal-boundary geometry or parcel elevation evidence without the required title/survey evidence.
